description: Defines the exact mathematical algorithms for transforming raw evidence into subskill confidence, skill scores, and role readiness. Single source of truth for numeric scoring.

single_source_of_truth_hierarchy.evidence_base_strengths: Section base_strength values are authoritatively defined in cv.json and linkedin.json. Engine.json references them dynamically.
single_source_of_truth_hierarchy.subskill_definitions: Subskills and composite keys are authoritatively defined in skills/*.json.
single_source_of_truth_hierarchy.role_importance_weights: Skill importance weights and readiness thresholds are authoritatively defined in roles/**/*.json.
single_source_of_truth_hierarchy.scoring_logic: This file (engine.json) is the sole authority for mathematical aggregation formulas, ceilings, and denominator isolation rules.

step_1_evidence_to_subskill_confidence.description: Transforms multi-source evidence signals into a single subskill confidence score (0.0 to 1.0).

rules.primary_signal: The single highest effective_strength signal across all valid sources.
rules.secondary_signals: All remaining signals for this subskill, weighted by diminishing_factor (0.10).

source_type_ceilings.description: Hard cap on maximum achievable subskill confidence based on the strongest evidence source present.

trigger_conditions.assessment_present: Requires at least one assessment signal with effective_strength >= 0.5. Weak signals do not unlock this ceiling.
trigger_conditions.github_present: Requires at least one github signal with effective_strength >= 0.5. Weak github signals (e.g., trivial .gitignore files) do not unlock this ceiling and will default to the self_reported_skills_and_summary ceiling.

section_to_ceiling_mapping_table.description: Complete, exhaustive mapping of every CV and LinkedIn section to its corresponding source_type_ceiling category.

assessment_scoring_and_override_rules.description: Rules for direct verification via assessment.

keyword_match_thresholds.notes: Ratio of expected keywords present in candidate answer text. >= 0.60 triggers correct_answer strength, 0.30 to 0.59 triggers partial_answer strength, < 0.30 triggers incorrect_answer verified_gap.

partial_answer.notes: Partial credit is blended into the confidence calculation as a signal of strength equal to the partial weight.

incorrect_answer.notes: If a candidate attempts an assessment question for a subskill and answers incorrectly, confidence is HARD SET to 0.00 (verified gap). No residual score from CV or LinkedIn is retained. This ALSO strictly applies to GitHub evidence: assessment is the final arbiter of truth in this system. A candidate may have copied code or used templates without understanding them; failing an assessment proves a lack of conceptual grasp, which supersedes repository contents.

worked_example.scenario: User has 2 CV skills_list entries (base_strength 0.3, modifier 0.5 -> effective 0.15) and 3 LinkedIn endorsements (base_strength 0.15, modifier 0.33 -> effective 0.05) for docker.dockerfile, but NO GitHub code and NO Assessment.
calculation: Ceiling category for CV skills_list & LinkedIn endorsements = 'self_reported_skills_and_summary' (0.30)

step_2_subskill_to_skill_score.description: Aggregates composite key subskill confidences ({skill_id}.{subskill_id}) into a skill score for a target role level.

subskill_categorization_by_level.expected_subskills: Subskills assigned to the target level or lower levels. These form the REQUIRED baseline. Included in denominator.
subskill_categorization_by_level.bonus_subskills: Subskills assigned to higher levels than the target level. Excluded from denominator. Only add bonus points if present.

formula.base_score: base_score = sum(confidence_i × weight_i) / sum(weight_i)  [for all expected_subskills]
formula.bonus_score: bonus_score = sum(confidence_j × 0.15)  [for higher_level subskills with confidence > 0.0]

denominator_isolation_rule.rule: Higher-level (bonus) subskills MUST NEVER be included in the denominator sum(weight_i). An un-evidenced senior subskill (confidence = 0.0) contributes 0 to bonus_score and 0 to the denominator. It causes ZERO penalty when scoring a Junior or Mid candidate.
denominator_isolation_rule.missing_expected_subskill_penalty: If an EXPECTED subskill has status 'not_yet_evidenced' (confidence = 0.0), it contributes 0.0 to the numerator but its weight (1.0 or 0.8) REMAINS in the denominator, correctly lowering the candidate's base score.

step_3_skill_to_role_readiness.description: Combines skill scores with role importance weights into a final Career Readiness Score (0.0 to 1.0).

threshold_evaluation.rule: Readiness score is evaluated against role thresholds using INCLUSIVE min and EXCLUSIVE max bounds, except for the top tier which is inclusive on 1.0.

composite_key_standard.rule: ALL references to subskills across ALL files (evidence source maps_to, skill definitions, AI outputs, scoring engine internals, API payloads) MUST use composite key format: '{skill_id}.{subskill_id}'. Bare subskill IDs are STRICTLY PROHIBITED.

evidence_status_meanings.evidence_found: At least one valid signal detected. Subskill confidence > 0.0.
evidence_status_meanings.not_yet_evidenced: No signals found from any scanned source. Confidence = 0.0. Does NOT mean the user lacks the skill; triggers adaptive assessment.
evidence_status_meanings.verified_gap: Targeted assessment was attempted and candidate failed. Confidence hard-set to 0.00. Identifies explicit learning gap.
